Documentation/Doppio

Rust UI frontend (Iced)

Stable Doppio Last verified: 2026-11-21 Source: doppio/

Architecture of the active Rust/Iced editor: workspace, panels, components, the C ABI boundary and the checks that keep it coherent.

Status: the active editor. caffeine-core is built without ImGui/ImNodes; the ImGui draw-list adapters live in caffeine-editor-support. The Rust workspace under doppio/ is the live Doppio frontend and talks to the engine through libcaffeine-capi. The old C++ editor is frozen in doppio-archived/ and is no longer part of the CMake build.

Why Iced#

  • MIT licensed, suitable for an engine/editor that other people may redistribute.
  • wgpu renderer, PaneGrid docking, dynamic widget trees in plain Rust.
  • Official iced_test headless simulator (click, typewrite, find, snapshots) for deterministic CI tests.
  • iced-mcp (MIT, iced 0.14) exposes the running widget tree to agents over MCP: snapshots, clicks, typing, assertions, flows and run-suite.

Workspace#

text
doppio/
  crates/engine/            libloading bindings to libcaffeine-capi
  crates/ui/
    src/windows/            main.rs (app state + PaneGrid), projectloader.rs
    src/uikit/components/   button, panel, toolbar, status, text_field, field_editor,
                            tree_view, component_card/picker, viewport_surface,
                            viewport_shader, rendering_canvas, gizmo, scene_markers,
                            viewport_math, asset_preview,
                            breadcrumb, code_editor
    src/uikit/theme.rs      colours, borders and spacing for the whole workspace
    src/uikit/panels/       hierarchy, sceneviewport, assetmanager, asset_wizard,
                            inspector, console, material, material_generator,
                            texture_generator, texture_set, nature_generator,
                            water_generator, terrain_generator, project_manager,
                            script, dryad_nodes
    src/uikit/project.rs    project.caffeine manifest, recursive scan, recent list
    src/uikit/script.rs     open script documents, editor buffers and save/revert
    src/uikit/dryad.rs      Dryad graph, catalog, emitter, .node.json and round-trip
  • App/UI state lives in windows/main.rs; panels and components are reusable library modules.
  • Panels compose components; they never build interactive widgets inline. Text fields, field editors, component cards/pickers and buttons live in uikit/components/; scripts/check-rust-ui.sh rejects raw text_input, checkbox, pick_list, slider or button calls in uikit/panels/.
  • The UI crates never touch FFI directly: only doppio-engine loads the shared library.
  • a four-region PaneGrid layout: Hierarchy on the left; Viewport (+ Material, Texture and other generators, Texture Set, Script, Dryad Nodes) in the centre; Material, Nature, Water and Terrain are editors, so they are tabs of the centre workspace); Inspector (+ Profiler, Photon, Environment, Audio) alone on the right, only what stays open while working; and a Project-style bottom dock with Assets (folder tree + file grid) next to the Console, tall enough to keep the Hierarchy short (a tab strip wider than its pane scrolls sideways and the pane drops its split button, so tabs are never hidden);
  • docking: dragging a tab away from its header shows guides on every pane (uikit/components/dock_overlay.rs): the centre adds the tab to that pane's group, the edge guides split the pane and dock on that side. Panes also have a maximise/restore button; open menus only close on a click outside, Escape or choosing an item (hover updates from widgets behind never dismiss them);
  • the Performance tab (uikit/panels/performance.rs, windows/main/performance.rs, View → Performance): where the render options live. The scene's Forward Render Features component (instancing, occlusion culling, reflection probes and screen-space reflections, volumetric light, diffuse sky light and their numbers; Add render features puts it on a new entity) and the editor viewport's own render scale, anti-aliasing, light shadows and ground grid. Scene edits are undo steps; viewport options are the editor's and are not. The editor starts the viewport at render scale 1.0 (the engine's own default stays 1.5 for other hosts). Agents use performance, performance_set, performance_add and show_performance. Photon keeps its own tab. With Photon off, or its component disabled, no Photon pass runs (a test checks the engine's profiler), though a profiler row keeps the totals since the last Reset;
  • building the editor: the editor lays out and draws the whole window on every tick, so an unoptimised build costs a full core and leaves the GPU waiting (a scene the engine draws in 2 ms ran at 7 fps). The workspace's Cargo.toml therefore builds dependencies at opt-level = 3 and the editor crates at 1 even in the dev profile, with line-table debug info; the first build takes minutes, later ones are incremental, and the whole-window layout dropped from about 20 ms to about 3 ms;
  • Play and the scene views: ▶ / ⏸ and ⏹ sit in the middle of the top bar (uikit/components/transport.rs, windows/main/sceneview.rs). Play snapshots the scene and starts the engine's game simulation (C ABI v23, GameSimulation): the systems caffeine-runtime runs between frames (animation, effects, fluids, navigation, 2D and 3D physics, Lua and Dryad scripts, procedural worlds, UI) over the editor's own world, shown in the Gameplay tab through the scene's active camera with the keyboard and pointer reaching the scripts. Pause freezes it, Stop ends it and puts the scene back as it was: what the game did, and anything edited meanwhile, is undone, and Play leaves no undo history. The Camera tab shows the scene through the selected Camera 3D (or the active one) without playing. Both pictures are engine scene views with their own render target and draw on demand like the editor viewport. The simulation does not belong to one view: the game ticks whichever tab is on screen, and the clock of the picture (clouds, weather, wind, water, sound) steps once per game tick by whichever view draws first (the editor Viewport, Gameplay or Camera), so every visible view shows the same moment and none counts it twice; with none on screen the physics and scripts go on and only the picture-bound parts wait. The engine's profiler lists the work: Game::tick with Game::animation, effects, physics2d, physics3d, scripts and world_and_ui, and SceneView::game / SceneView::camera. Agents use toggle_play, stop_play, game_key, show_gameplay, show_camera_preview and the play query;
  • detaching: the ⧉ button in a pane's title bar turns the active tab into a window of its own (the editor runs as an iced::daemon; windows/main/detach.rs). A detached tab is the same view over the same engine and documents, so nothing is copied: it leaves the dock layout and is drawn in another operating-system window with a Dock back button. Closing that window docks the tab back, closing the main window quits, a "show this tab" command raises the window instead of docking a second copy, and the last tab of the editor cannot leave. Agents use detach_tab, attach_tab and the windows query; the single-window agent bridge build refuses to detach;
  • the Assets wizard (+ New / Import in the Assets toolbar, uikit/asset_wizard.rs + uikit/panels/asset_wizard.rs): Create (folder, Lua, Dryad script; material and texture set open their editors), Import (copies files or folders into the current folder, never overwriting; the queue tags every file with its kind and flags the ones that will be skipped; a file dropped on the window outside the wizard is imported straight into the folder being browsed) and Pack (caf-pack --input <asset root> --output <project>.cap, found via CAF_PACK, CAFFEINE_ENGINE_ROOT, a sibling caf-pack/build/src or PATH);
  • the file browser (uikit/file_browser.rs + uikit/panels/file_browser.rs, Browse… in the Import tab): Doppio's own picker for files and folders on this computer, identical on Linux, macOS and Windows and drivable by tests and agents because it is plain std::fs (no operating-system dialog). It has places (home, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, every drive on Windows, / and the mount points elsewhere), a path trail, a box that takes typed or pasted paths (~, relative, quoted, file://), a name filter, hidden-file and importable-types switches and a multi-selection that survives walking between folders; a double-clicked file is taken at once and the next Browse opens where the last one ended;
  • asset kinds, cards and the shared picker: uikit/asset_kind.rs is the one table of file extensions (textures including bmp/psd/pnm, meshes, audio including flac, fonts, prefabs, scenes, terrain/water/nature graphs, texture sets and data files such as .json, .csv, .mtl and .bin); the Assets grid draws a card per asset with a bar in its kind's colour, a thumbnail or icon well and an extension chip. Every asset field composes asset_field (thumbnail, editable path, … and ×) and opens the single asset.pick.* overlay: matching assets with kind filters, search, the current value first and a None row. Inspector string fields are recognised by name (Mesh Path, Clip Path, Script…); the Terrain and Water Generator slots use it too; agents drive it with asset_pick_* and asset_kinds. Whatever is typed or picked goes through the engine's asset manager first (windows/main/assetref.rs, C ABI 24): a file from outside the project is imported into its folder and the field keeps the project path, a file of the wrong kind is refused before anything is copied, and a path still being typed is kept as typed. The Material Generator's Image and Normal Map nodes, the Terrain and Water slots, the Nature material and image nodes and the baking of a graph follow the same rule;
  • stable widget ids for the toolbar, inspector inputs and entity rows;
  • a headless iced_test harness covering editing, panes, console filters, hierarchy search, viewport gestures and flight;
  • an optional agent feature that routes main through iced_mcp::run.

The C++ boundary:

  • caffeine-core: engine only, no ImGui/ImNodes.
  • caffeine-editor-support: ImGui adapters for engine render helpers.
  • caffeine-capi: the C ABI used by Rust (and any other external frontend).

Run it with:

bash
cd doppio
cargo run -p doppio-ui -- ../assets/benchmarks/dense_outdoor.caf

Materials, procedural library and real depth: materials-guide.md. The current widget catalogue and screenshots are published as the UI reference.

Drive and inspect the UI without a window (any agent, CI or human; plain JSON over stdin/stdout, see headless-testing.md):

bash
./scripts/doppio-headless.sh widgets                      # what is on screen
./scripts/doppio-headless.sh run doppio/tests/ui-flows --format text
./scripts/doppio-headless.sh screenshot --annotate --out /tmp/shots

Run the checks used by CI/agents:

bash
./scripts/check-rust-ui.sh
# cargo fmt --check, cargo test, cargo check --features agent, clippy -D warnings
# plus the caffeine-core ImGui coupling audit

Migration status#

Engine / ImGui split — done#

  • caffeine-core builds without ImGui/ImNodes; nm reports 0 ImGui/ImNodes symbols in libcaffeine-core.a.
  • caffeine-editor-support contains the engine ImGui adapters (Overlay2D::draw, SkyboxRenderer).
  • 18 UI-kit headers and 1 editor-UI header still reference ImGui; that is the legacy SDK/editor side, not core.
  • caffeine-runtime is still an ImGui frontend and needs an RHI render path before it can be made UI-free.

Measure the coupling with:

bash
python3 scripts/audit_core_ui_coupling.py
python3 scripts/audit_core_ui_coupling.py --fail-on-leaks

C ABI / data-oriented boundary — first slice done#

  • header: include/caffeine/capi/EngineAPI.h
  • implementation: src/caffeine/capi/EngineAPI.cpp
  • version: CAFFEINE_CAPI_VERSION 2; caffeine_capi_version() is exposed to frontends and shown as a status-bar badge.
  • test: tests/test_capi.cpp ([capi], 318 assertions / 13 cases)
  • opaque CaffeineSession, CaffeineEntity and versioned CaffeineResult;
  • session create/destroy and .caf scene load;
  • entity count/list/name, create, destroy, rename and selection;
  • position/rotation/scale get/set (setting a transform creates one when the entity has none), plus resolved world positions (entity_world_position, set_entity_world_position) so groups compose position, rotation and scale; the offscreen renderer calls Scene::propagateTransforms every frame before drawing;
  • dirty state and .caf save; the Rust toolbar has Save + a dirty marker;
  • project asset listing (set_asset_root, refresh_assets, asset_at); the Rust Asset Manager shows real files and a file count;
  • hierarchy links (entity_parent, set_entity_parent) with cycle rejection; the Hierarchy + opens a create-entity palette with built-in prefabs (empty/folder, mesh primitives, lights, camera, physics props, player, terrain/water) plus a duplicate-selection recipe. Prefabs are applied through the same C ABI components and are undoable;
  • the Hierarchy panel composes the reusable tree_view component: compact full-width rows, semantic icons, expand/collapse chevrons, hover/selection states and per-row context menus. Rows are draggable: dropping one onto another reparents it, and dropping it on the scene root unparents it. The Assets browser shares the breadcrumb, text field and asset-preview components;
  • PBR material assets (.mat): CaffeineMaterial mirrors the engine surface (albedo, metallic, roughness, reflectance, emission, transmission, clearcoat, sheen, iridescence, reflection and UV tiling/offset), load/save, built-in presets, assignment to the selected entity's Mesh Filter and a synchronous sphere preview rendered by MaterialPreviewRenderer. caffeine_texture_generate_map derives normal, AO, roughness, metallic and height maps; caffeine_texture_pack_maps writes ORM, Unity HDRP mask and Unity metallic-smoothness packings; caffeine_texture_save_rgba writes generator output. asset_path, asset_project_path and resolve_path bridge asset-relative, project-relative and absolute paths;
  • component schema and values (component_type_*, entity_component_*, add/remove_component); the Inspector is generic and edits every registered component (Transform, Camera 3D, lights, renderers, physics, colliders, scripts) with scalar, vector, bool, string and enum fields;
  • Dryad preview (caffeine_session_run_dryad) runs onCreate + one onUpdate on an entity without entering play mode; caffeine_dryad_available reports whether the interpreter was linked;
  • non-blocking render (render_begin / render_poll): submit a download copy and poll its fence instead of waiting for the GPU;
  • in-memory scene snapshots (snapshot / restore): the whole world serialized to bytes, used by the editor undo/redo timeline;
  • camera get/set (CaffeineCamera), driven by viewport gestures and WASD;
  • viewport settings (set/get_viewport_settings): reference grid, FXAA/TAA and internal render scale;
  • tick/frame-stat bookkeeping (systems will be wired incrementally);
  • no ImGui and no editor headers in the ABI;
  • libcaffeine-capi.so shared library (CMake target caffeine-capi);
  • a libloading Rust bridge in doppio/crates/engine/src/lib.rs, with a round-trip integration test that skips when the library is absent;
  • the Rust Inspector shows the real C++ position and can nudge it with +X;
  • 222 Rust tests: 2 engine bridge/snapshot tests, 3 material-preview integration tests, 216 UI/widget tests (1 ignored docs generator) and 1 doctest.

The app loads a real scene through the ABI:

bash
cd doppio
cargo run -p doppio-ui -- ../assets/benchmarks/dense_outdoor.caf

The hierarchy then shows the real C++ entities (Rock/Tree/...). Without the shared library it falls back to fake data, so UI tests do not depend on CMake.

Still to add before the Rust UI is fully wired:

  • component schemas and field snapshots in POD arrays;
  • commands/undo/redo/play-pause and remaining asset operations;
  • events (dirty state, selection, logs, asset changes).

The existing PluginHostApi is a good function-table precedent. The existing DOPPIO_TEST_MODE JSON loop (TestRequestHandler) is a good engine-side test precedent.

Component schema and generic Inspector#

  • The C ABI exposes a component catalog (id, name, fields with kind/limits/ enum options) plus per-entity instances and field get/set/add/remove.
  • The registry covers Transform, Position/Rotation/Scale 3D, Camera 3D, Light plus directional/point/spot, Mesh Renderer, Mesh Filter, Rigid Body 3D/2D, Collider 3D/2D and Script.
  • The Inspector is generic but composed as a property editor: an entity header, a combined Transform card (position/rotation/scale axes), collapsible component cards with icons and compact remove actions, striped property rows, right-aligned labels, sliders with values, vector axis groups and a colour picker. Each component has a compact remove button and the pane has an Add Component picker. Every edit is an undo step.
  • The panel itself only composes uikit components (text_field, field_editor, component_card, component_picker); it contains no raw text_input/checkbox/pick_list. scripts/check-rust-ui.sh enforces it.
  • Window chrome is a menu bar (Scene, Edit, View) plus status chips; every pane body is wrapped by the panel component with a title and muted subtitle. Colours and spacing come from uikit/theme.rs (the check rejects hardcoded colours outside it).
  • Prefer direct manipulation over button rows: hierarchy rows support click, double-click (focus) and right-click (context menu: add/focus/delete); viewport gestures are drag/pan/wheel/double-click/right-click. Menu entries and Ctrl shortcuts cover the rest.

Project Manager and Assets#

  • When no .caf scene is passed on the command line, Doppio opens its own Project Manager over the workspace (the editor fixtures and screenshot runs pass a scene, so they stay deterministic). The Project menu and Ctrl+O reopen it at any time.
  • The launcher may also pass a project root or project.caffeine as the first argument. Doppio opens it directly, sets the engine asset root, loads last_scene and shows the active-project chip instead of the startup dialog.
  • The manager has Create New, Open Recent and Browse Projects tabs, mirroring the archived startup dialog. Create validates the name, creates Assets/Raw/{Animations,Audio,Generators,Materials,Models,Prefabs,Sky,TextureSets,Textures}, Assets/Processed, Scripts, scenes, materials, texture_sets and build, writes project.caffeine and opens the project. Browse recursively scans a folder up to six levels for project.caffeine, and Recent reads ~/.config/caffeine/recent.txt ($CAFFEINE_RECENT_PROJECTS overrides the file for tests and portable runs). Rows select on click and open on double-click; the primary action opens the selection.
  • Opening a project sets the engine asset root from paths.assets_raw, loads last_scene when it exists, or clears the world and saves a starter scenes/main.caf for a new project. Saving the scene updates last_scene in the manifest. The active project is shown as a chip in the title bar.
  • The manifest format is the existing project.caffeine JSON shape (project_name, engine_version, paths, template_type, last_scene), so projects created by the C++ tools and by Doppio are interchangeable. uikit::project owns create/load/scan/recent helpers and injects the recent file in tests so no real user state is touched.
  • The Sample template is the fixed project the team benchmarks and tries Doppio in: the standard folders and nothing else, named Sample unless a name is typed. Its canonical copy is samples/Sample in the engine repository, and a test fails when the template and that copy drift apart (cargo test -p doppio-ui zz_write_sample -- --ignored rewrites it).
  • The Assets pane is now a real browser: clickable breadcrumbs, Up/Root, refresh, folder-first navigation and a Grid/List switch. Folder navigation is derived from AssetInfo.relative_path; no new C ABI call is required. Search walks the whole asset root (not only the current folder), thumbnails and material tints are reused, and the existing internal drag/drop path keeps original asset indices so dropping a .mat or image on the Hierarchy or Inspector still works.

Script editor and Dryad nodes#

  • The Script pane opens .lua and .dyd files as tabs, with per-file dirty tracking, Save/Revert/Close, line numbers, syntax colouring and the shared project path. Scripts open from Assets (single-click for .lua; double-click for the source of a .dyd), the Scene menu, Ctrl+Shift+E, or the MCP open_script action.
  • Iced 0.14's stock text_editor paints empty under this workspace's renderer, so uikit/components/code_editor.rs wraps the canvas-based iced-code-editor widget. The pane still owns the document state, dirty checks and disk I/O; the component is the only place that knows the editor implementation.
  • Attach Selected writes the script's project-relative path into the selected entity's Script component (adding the component when missing); Detach clears it. Both are undoable scene edits.
  • The Dryad Nodes pane (Ctrl+Shift+D, Scene menu, or a .dyd asset) edits the same .dyd plus its sibling .node.json. The Rust dryad module matches the C++ NodeEmitter/NodeGraphIO/NodeRoundTrip formats byte-for-byte: deterministic // @node markers, sorted JSON ids/edges and %.17g numbers. It supports OnUpdate, Set/Get Position, Set/Get Scale, Translate, DeltaTime, Constant, Branch and Log, plus the runtime nodes Key Down, Action Down, Input Axis (name in the properties panel), Total Time and Destroy Self, with typed exec/data ports, connection validation, inline input fallbacks, Add motion and Sync from .dyd. The new nodes exist in the Rust catalog only; the C++ NodeCatalog (archived editor) still lists the original ten.
  • Reference tooltip. Hovering a name in the Script pane shows its signature and description in a floating card. uikit/script_reference.rs holds one table per language (Lua caffeine.*, Dryad caffeine_*); a test reads the C++ binding sources and fails when a Dryad native is missing from the table. .dyd files use the JavaScript grammar for colouring (Dryad is a brace language); colouring of the engine API names themselves is not available because iced-code-editor does not take a custom grammar.
  • Attach and Run once reuse the script component and the C ABI caffeine_session_run_dryad preview (onCreate + one onUpdate). Saving the graph writes both files; opening a .dyd also stages its source in the Script pane for hand editing. Sources without // @node markers stay valid Dryad and the graph editor reports the mismatch instead of rewriting them.

Material studio#

  • .mat files are first-class assets. Clicking a .mat in Assets opens the Material pane (a tab beside the Inspector); clicking a texture creates an unsaved material whose albedo map points at it. The pane is a reusable panels/material composition of material_preview, texture_slot, card, slider, color_picker, dropdown and checkbox components.
  • The preview is a real engine-rendered sphere (caffeine_session_render_material_preview), 256 px, throttled to ~8 Hz and only while the pane is visible. Dragging the image orbits it. The preview renderer has its own targets, so it never resizes the scene viewport target.
  • Surface controls cover the full CAFMAT3 surface: albedo/alpha, metallic, roughness, reflectance, emission, alpha mode/cutoff, UV tiling/offset, normal/AO strength, transmission/IOR, clearcoat, sheen, iridescence and reflection. Presets keep the material name, maps and UV layout. Normal maps can be marked DirectX (green down); the renderer flips green before tangent space shading.
  • Texture slots (albedo, normal, ORM, emission) open a searchable project picker with image thumbnails. The Assets pane filters to textures, materials, meshes and scenes and has its own search field, so a material or map is a few keystrokes away instead of scrolling through source files. Material cards fall back to an albedo swatch when a thumbnail cannot be decoded.
  • The map baker writes beside the saved .mat: normal from a height/colour source (OpenGL or DirectX green), AO from ring-average cavity, roughness (inverted albedo luminance) and metallic (bright-surface mask), then packs ORM, Unity HDRP mask or Unity metallic-smoothness. Generated normal/ORM maps are assigned back to the material; Unity packings are export-only because the renderer's ORM slot expects R=AO, G=roughness, B=metallic.
  • The Inspector shows a compact Material slot for the selected entity's Mesh Filter; clicking it opens the material, × unassigns it (undoable).
  • Apply assigns the open material through the C ABI (undo step Assign Material). Scene edits never rewrite .mat files, and material edits stay unsaved until Save.
  • Texture paths are stored project-relative, as existing scene/material files do. asset_path, asset_project_path and resolve_path bridge asset browser paths, .mat paths and absolute paths; MeshCache also accepts the sample materials' repository-relative assets/... prefix.
  • The workflow follows the public conventions used by TextureCraft and MaterialCraft (PBR channels, texture slots, ORM/Unity packing, live preview) but is implemented from Caffeine's own C ABI and renderer; no reference code or assets were copied.

Material generator (node canvas)#

  • uikit/components/node_canvas.rs is a reusable canvas component: nodes are graph-space cards with typed input/output ports, cubic wires, selection, node dragging, empty-space panning and wheel zoom. It emits Select, MoveNode, Connect and Viewport events; the caller owns the graph model. The same component can back other node tools.
  • uikit/generators.rs is a small clean-room atomic graph: Color, Image, Normal Map, Noise (value/Perlin), Voronoi (cells/distance), Checker, Bricks, Gradient, Blend (13 modes plus a scalar mask input), Normal Blend (whiteout/ linear), Levels, Curve, HSL, Threshold, Blur, Sharpen, Emboss, Directional Blur, Edge/Cavity/Distance masks, Warp, Value, Luminance, Dot, an Output node with Color/Roughness/Metallic/Height/AO inputs and imported Unknown placeholders. Ports are typed colour/scalar; scalar inputs read the luminance of connected colour maps and fall back to Output constants. Evaluation is CPU, tileable at 128–2048 px, cycle-safe and memoized; 2K is the safe max until the evaluator gets a tiled/parallel 4K path.
  • The Generator tab (opened from Material → Generate…, the Scene menu, or the MCP action) puts the palette, canvas and selected-node properties side by side and maximizes the pane while editing. Image and Normal Map nodes use the shared texture picker and support UV/planar/tri-planar/cylindrical/spherical projection, tiling, offset, linear/nearest filtering and clamp/repeat wrapping. Bake to Material runs on a worker thread with progress and cancel; image decoding also happens on that worker. The progress bar follows the reachable nodes, then reports Packing maps, Baking occlusion, Writing maps and Done, so the final AO and map packing no longer look stuck at the last node. Occlusion uses a separable box blur (O(pixels) instead of O(pixels × radius)), which keeps 2K bakes fast. It writes <material>_gen_base_<bits>.png, height/roughness/metallic/packed maps, derives a normal map from height and assigns the maps to the open .mat before marking it unsaved. A successful bake now saves the .mat and assigns it to the selected entity automatically, so the 3D viewport and the generator's 3D PREVIEW (the live material preview sphere) show exactly what the graph produced. The generator's OUTPUT PREVIEW is a low-resolution live bake of the Output node, refreshed after each graph edit with a 160 ms debounce; no manual bake is needed to see parameter/brick/mask changes. Direct specular is energy-normalised and the height field darkens direct, ambient, IBL and reflected light (and point/spot POM shadows), so a face pointing at the sun keeps its grooves instead of flattening to a white plastic plate. Every node also shows a live 72 px thumbnail of its own evaluated output, computed in the same worker pass. The right-hand panel edits the channel-packing preset/sources, saves named user presets and chooses 8/16-bit output.
  • Saving a material also writes its <name>.mgraph sidecar (versioned text) beside the .mat; reopening restores nodes, links, parameters, positions and resolution. Graphs are per material, not shared session state.
  • Graph edits have their own snapshot timeline (GraphHistory), separate from scene undo. Add/delete node, connect, disconnect, move, parameters, resolution, copy/paste, image assignment and reroute dots are undoable; drags and repeated parameter changes coalesce. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y route to graph history while the Generator pane is active, and the header has ↶/↷ buttons.
  • Wires are hit-tested as bézier curves. Clicking selects a wire (the properties panel offers Delete link); right-click deletes it; dragging a connected input detaches its source so it can be dropped on another input. Double-clicking a wire inserts a pass-through Dot reroute node, with the original source and target rewired in one undo step.
  • The palette uses the shared tree_view grouped by category (Textures, Generators, Filters, Utilities, Output), with collapsible groups and search filtering. Nodes snap to a 16-unit grid (toggle), Fit frames the whole graph, and Copy/Paste duplicates the selected node with a 24-unit offset.
  • node_canvas ignores mouse presses whose cursor is outside its bounds unless a drag is already active, so clicking property sliders never starts an empty-canvas pan or clears the selected node.
  • The Material panel's AO from scene button calls Photon's BVH/GPU AO bake for the selected entity and assigns the resulting ORM map to the open material (caffeine_session_bake_ao).
  • uikit/materialcraft.rs reads/writes portable .mcmat archives (ZIP with material.json, cooked maps and source.sbs), parses the SBS XML subset and exports a minimal SBS source that is re-imported and checked before writing. Unknown filters/outputs become Unknown placeholder nodes with warnings.
  • uikit/materialcraft_io.rs maps imported maps into a .mat (packing separate AO/roughness/metallic maps into ORM) and writes .sbs, .mgraph and map files. The editor exposes MCP import_materialcraft / export_materialcraft; the headless binary is doppio-material.
  • The generator follows MaterialCraft's public primitive-editor workflow (palette → canvas → properties, typed ports, output node, live baked maps) without sharing its code, node definitions or assets.
  • The remaining material/texture/generator work is tracked in material-pipeline.md: scene/geometry bakes, MaterialCraft SBS import and TextureCraft-style texture sets/painting.

Texture sets (TextureCraft-style foundation)#

  • uikit/texture_set.rs owns UDIM tiles 1001–1010, six default channels (baseColor, roughness, metallic, height, AO, curvature), paint/fill layers, per-tile layer masks, brush settings, compositing and per-tile undo snapshots.
  • The Texture Set pane (Material toolbar → Texture Set, or the MCP new_texture_set action) stacks tiles/layers on the left, a reusable uv_canvas in the centre and channels/brush/export controls on the right. The pane maximizes while painting; Material restores the normal layout.
  • uv_canvas paints RGBA or layer-mask dabs with brush radius, hardness, opacity and colour. 3D paint toggles viewport painting: pick_uv in the C ABI ray-picks the selected mesh against the editor camera and returns the hit UV; strokes are written to the active tile/layer and the resulting base colour is applied to the entity for viewport feedback.
  • AO from height and Curvature bake new layers; AO from scene calls Photon and imports the ORM red channel. Normal, Position and ID call caffeine_session_bake_mesh_map and import world-normal, world-position or object-ID UV maps into matching channels. All imports keep per-tile undo.
  • The .texset project is a ZIP with texture-set.json, RGBA PNG tiles and grayscale mask PNGs. TileHistory snapshots only the affected tile (cap 64) so undo never copies the whole project.
  • Export presets: separate PBR maps, glTF ORM and Unity HDRP mask. The doppio-material texset-* CLI and MCP export_texture_set use the same code.

Phase 5 polish#

  • Material preview: sphere/cube/plane subjects, HDRI path + exposure controls, and an asynchronous begin/poll readback (render_material_preview_begin / _poll) so orbit drags and edits do not block the UI. It renders at 512 px and uses contain-fit with a wider camera so the subject is never cropped. The old synchronous entry point remains for tools and tests.
  • Thumbnails now decode through the engine (caffeine_texture_load_thumbnail) before falling back to Iced's path loader, which fixes PNG/JPG/HDR assets that Iced could not decode. The asset grid, material slots and pickers share this path; the cache is keyed by resolved path + modification stamp so refreshing an asset list only re-decodes thumbnails that changed.
  • Inspector Choose material… opens the searchable .mat picker. Assets can be dragged from the Assets grid onto a Hierarchy entity (material assignment or material-from-texture) or onto Material map slots (texture assignment). OS file drops still assign .mat/textures and import mesh files.
  • uikit/mesh_material_import.rs imports OBJ/MTL and .gltf/.glb materials (albedo, normal, occlusion, roughness/metallic factors and maps, emission, alpha and KHR_texture_transform UV tiling/offset) into .mat assets and writes an .mgraph sidecar with an Image node for albedo. MCP import_mesh_materials and file drop use the same importer.
  • Material badges show map presence with decoded resolution or missing, plus the normal convention and alpha mode; the status bar shows the C ABI version (now v2).
  • Apply material saves the open material first, so baked generator maps and complex masks reach the .mat file before assignment. Applying to an entity without a Mesh Filter now creates a visible cube preview mesh instead of failing silently.

Undo and redo#

  • doppio/crates/ui/src/history.rs keeps a timeline of editor states: the UI entity list, an optional engine snapshot, the dirty flag and the selection.
  • States are full scene snapshots rather than per-field commands, so undo also covers components the UI does not edit yet.
  • Steps are named (Add Entity 3, Rename Boss, Move Rock to x=…), typing in one field coalesces into a single step, and a new edit drops the redo branch.
  • Cap: 200 steps / ~128 MB; the oldest steps are dropped first.
  • Toolbar Undo/Redo, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y, and MCP undo / redo actions. The history query returns the timeline, cursor and can-undo/redo.
  • Snapshot restore remaps entity ids, so the UI re-reads the hierarchy; the serializer writes and recreates entities in stable id order to preserve it.

Viewport — asynchronous CPU readback#

  • RenderDevice::initOffscreen() creates a headless SDL_GPU device.
  • caffeine_session_render() is the blocking path (tools/tests): render with GpuSceneRenderer::renderWithCamera into an RGBA8 target and read it back.
  • caffeine_session_render_begin() renders, starts a texture→transfer-buffer download and returns immediately with a fence. RenderDevice::endOffscreen() does not call SDL_WaitForGPUIdle; the C API keeps one offscreen frame in flight and releases upload buffers when its readback fence signals.
  • caffeine_session_render_poll() returns PENDING until the fence is signalled, then maps the transfer buffer and copies the pixels.
  • The transfer buffer is reused across frames instead of being allocated and destroyed every frame. A 33 ms render interval and a once-per-second HUD update keep the UI thread from being flooded.
  • Finished frames are drawn by uikit/components/viewport_shader.rs, not by a new Iced image handle per frame. The shader owns one persistent wgpu texture and writes into it only when the frame id changes, so animated updates no longer create/destroy textures or flicker on the compositor.
  • doppio-engine::Engine::{render, render_begin, render_poll} wrap the ABI.
  • uikit/components/viewport_surface.rs owns the interactive surface: image or empty state, HUD chips (resolution, grid, latency, FPS, camera), mouse handling (left drag orbit, right/middle drag pan, wheel zoom, double-click focus) and grab/grabbing cursor feedback.
  • The scene viewport reports its real pane size through an Iced sensor; the app renders at 2x logical pixels (capped at 3 megapixels) so the image stays sharp after Iced scales it back down. The C ABI adds 1.5x internal supersampling and FXAA (TAA/off are also exposed), and enables the GPU reference grid with adaptive cell spacing and coloured X/Z axes. The grid fades out between 1,500 and 5,000 units of visible range: at extreme zoom its screen-space lines sit almost coplanar with distant terrain and alias into dashed confetti. The near plane also scales with orbit distance so a 50k far plane does not destroy depth precision. The View menu (or G over the viewport) toggles the grid.
  • WASD flies along the view direction, Q/E move vertically and Shift boosts speed. The camera focus is never height-clamped; the orbit pitch only stops just short of the pole so lookAt stays stable. That allows reaching cloud layers and orbiting beyond the old 5,000-unit zoom limit.
  • uikit/components/gizmo.rs draws the selected entity's transform gizmo over the shader surface using the same orbit camera projection (shared maths in components/viewport_math.rs). 1/2/3 (or View → Move/Rotate/Scale Tool) switch modes. Move has shaded 3D arrows and plane handles, Rotate has depth-shaded rings with a swept-angle wedge, and Scale follows the object's local axes and has a centre cube for uniform scale. The handle under the cursor is highlighted. Edits flow through the normal commit path and coalesce into one undo step per handle drag. The overlay projects the entity's resolved world position, so a child stays attached to a moved/rotated/scaled group, and move edits are converted back through the parent transform. It projects with the camera snapshot of the frame currently on screen, not the UI's newest camera, so an orbiting world and its gizmo stay aligned despite the asynchronous readback.
  • uikit/components/scene_markers.rs draws markers for entities that have no mesh: light rays, bulbs and cones, camera frustums, colliders and locators. They sit under the gizmo, can be clicked to select their entity and are toggled from the View menu. Details, limits and images: gizmos-and-markers.md.
  • ViewportTick still fires every 16 ms, but the viewport submits at most one frame per 33 ms; the HUD shows measured latency and a rolling FPS. The persistent shader texture is kept when a frame is unchanged, so dropped frames can never show a partial or empty viewport.
  • Camera maths (orbit, pan basis, fly movement, zoom, focus selection) lives in windows/main.rs; there is no camera button row. Gestures and shortcuts (Ctrl+F focus, Ctrl+0 reset, Ctrl+R render) drive it.

The viewport shows the real C++ scene (terrain, rocks, sky) in Iced.

Generators: a workspace and a notice#

The Nature, Water, Terrain and Texture tabs (and the Scatter action) share two services (windows/main/workspace.rs):

  • A workspace without a project. Generators write meshes, materials, terrains and plans as project assets. With no project open, App::ensure_workspace gives the engine a scratch project ($CAFFEINE_SCRATCH, else <data dir>/caffeine/doppio/scratch) the first time an action needs files, and says so; the files show in the Assets pane. The top bar shows a No project chip meanwhile. (Before this, Place in scene with no project answered with one small line in a side panel, and the Texture tab wrote to a Textures folder relative to the working directory.) The engine treats the scratch folder as the project root too (caffeine_session_set_asset_root sets the root when no scene has), because it resolves the relative asset paths the generators store against it; without that the placed tree was in the scene but drew nothing.
  • The project root is the folder with project.caffeine. caffeine_session_load_scene walks up from the scene (four levels) to the nearest project.caffeine, and only then falls back to the folder above a scenes / Scenes directory (Doppio creates Scenes/; the engine used to know only the lowercase name and took Scenes/ as the root). Its assets/raw lookup ignores case too (Assets/Raw). Generators store meshes as project paths (Assets/Raw/Models/Nature/oak_trunk.obj, from asset_project_path), like materials and textures, because the engine resolves a relative path against the project root, not the asset root. Every recipe write rescans the assets, so the file shows in the Assets pane at once.
  • A notice anyone can see. Every change of a generator's status line (and of the Scatter action's) becomes a chip in the top bar for 12 seconds and an entry in the Console, coloured by how it went (status::tone_for_text: success, warning for "placed with problems", danger for failures). The panels show the same line under their inspector, wrapped and coloured, through status::note.

Also in the generator tabs: the preset dropdown shows the preset in use (it used to read Choose… even with Oak loaded), graphs that load fit the canvas up to 1.4x, node titles and ports are larger and a parameter summary that would overlap a long title is left to the inspector, checkboxes put their label next to the box (checkbox::property, and checkbox::inline for toolbars), and the Place/Scatter controls live in the toolbar where a selected node's long parameter list cannot push them out of view. Tested by generators_work_without_a_project_and_say_what_happened, status_lines_get_a_tone_from_what_they_say and the flow generators-interconnect.json.

Console#

Entries are typed as Errors, Log, Actions, Engine or UI and prefixed in the list. The filter chips hide/show each category independently; the scrollable anchors to the newest entry.

Shortcuts#

Shortcut Action

Ctrl+N add empty entity
Ctrl+Shift+N open the create-entity palette
Ctrl+Shift+M new material
Ctrl+S save scene
Ctrl+Enter play / pause
Ctrl+F focus selection
Ctrl+0 reset camera
Ctrl+R render viewport now
G (over the viewport) toggle the reference grid
1 / 2 / 3 (over the viewport) move / rotate / scale gizmo
X (over the viewport) gizmo snapping on / off (0.25 m, 15°, 0.1)
W / A / S / D fly along the view / strafe
Q / E fly down / up

double-click hierarchy row or viewport focus selection

Why not a shared GPU texture yet#

SDL_GPU exposes no native resource handles (no VkImage, D3D12 resource or shared handle), so Iced/wgpu cannot import the engine's colour target through the public API. The async readback above removes the GPU stall; the copy remains. Real zero-copy requires one of:

  1. a wgpu RHI backend for the engine (or rendering the scene in wgpu directly);
  2. Vulkan external memory via a custom SDL_GPU patch/extension;
  3. an embedding strategy with a separate SDL3 viewport window.

Until then, keep the readback path responsive and treat the texture hand-off as a renderer-level project, not a UI change.

Plugins#

Plugins are C++ and draw ImGui. The Rust UI needs one of:

  • a legacy ImGui host window for old plugins; or
  • a plugin v2 contract (data/commands, optional process/WASM isolation).

This is the largest hidden cost and should be designed before removing ImGui from the runtime and the legacy SDK.

Tests and agents#

UI tests are Playwright-style but headless: they drive the real Iced widget tree, click by id, type into inputs, apply the resulting messages and assert on the next frame. No window, GPU or engine build is required.

  • crates/ui/src/windows/main/tests.rs has a Harness with click, type_into, shows, has, bounds, capture and wait_for, plus focused tests and one end-to-end editor_workflow scenario (add → select → rename → move → delete).
  • Fixtures (App::empty and two-entity editor) keep tests deterministic.

UI ids, bounds and visual captures#

Iced ids are flat strings, which does not scale to hundreds of widgets. Doppio uses a typed taxonomy in uikit::id:

text
group.subgroup.object        e.g. editor.toolbar.add_entity
                                  inspector.entity.name
                                  hierarchy.list.entity_row.3
                                  assets.grid.asset_card.7
  • UiId implements Into<iced::widget::Id>, so components take ids directly.
  • Static ids are constants (id::ADD_ENTITY, id::PANE_INSPECTOR, …).
  • List rows use id::entity_row(index) / id::asset_card(index); the group and subgroup stay stable while the object carries the index.
  • id::CATALOG documents every stable widget with a description and kind, and id::description(key) resolves dynamic rows too.
  • Panes are wrapped in an id'd container, so a screenshot can target editor.pane.inspector as naturally as a button.

The native harness exposes the layout of any id (Harness::bounds) and writes annotated PNGs:

  • Harness::capture(id, path, caption) crops a headless iced_test frame to the target, adds a highlight border and a caption rendered with the bundled JetBrains Mono (assets/jetbrains-mono/).
  • Harness::capture_group(&[(id, label)], …) crops the union of several widgets, draws numbered colored boxes and a legend — the "annotated panel" format.

The gallery generator walks the catalog, captures every widget that exists in the fixture, and writes images, a JSON manifest and English/Portuguese Markdown:

bash
./scripts/generate-doppio-ui-docs.sh            # doppio/target/doppio-ui-docs
./scripts/generate-doppio-ui-docs.sh --publish  # update caffeine-website

Descriptions and translations live in caffeine-website/captures/ui-captions.json, so an agent can improve the prose without touching Rust. The manifest (manifest.json) carries id/group/kind/bounds/image for each entry.

Agents get the same views through iced-mcp: snapshot returns ids and bounds, screenshot accepts a target id plus highlight (or a region) and saves a PNG, and ui_catalog lists the documented ids, groups and descriptions.

Agents (MCP)#

iced-mcp is behind the agent feature and attaches only when ICED_MCP=1:

bash
cargo install iced-mcp-server        # once
cd doppio
ICED_MCP=1 cargo run -p doppio-ui --features agent

The MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, any MCP client) launches the app, reads the widget tree (snapshot), clicks/types by id or text, records flows and replays them with iced-mcp run-suite. On top of the widget tools, Doppio registers scene-level queries and actions:

Kind Name What it does

query selection the selected entity (local transform and world_position)

Because every action is an iced Message, agents can only do what the UI can do, and the messages tool shows exactly what each call published. Agent edits are ordinary undo steps (undo / redo), and the history query exposes the timeline.

Visual regression#

doppio/.iced-mcp/scripts/visual-regression.luau captures the hierarchy, assets, inspector and console panes with screenshot_diff (the GPU viewport is excluded on purpose). Baselines are per-machine/GPU and live in .iced-mcp/baselines/, which is gitignored:

bash
./scripts/check-doppio-visual.sh --update-baselines  # seed on this machine/image
./scripts/check-doppio-visual.sh                     # CI check

The script skips cleanly without iced-mcp or a display. Commit baselines only from a controlled CI image if you want cross-machine visual diffs.

A full scripted session lives in doppio/.iced-mcp/scripts/editor-smoke.luau. material-smoke.luau covers opening a .mat, the rendered preview, assigning it to an entity, presets and texture slots; material-generator-smoke, materialcraft-smoke and texture-set-smoke cover the node canvas, portable round-trip and texture-set painting/export; project-smoke covers creating and reopening a project plus asset navigation; script-dryad-smoke covers the Script Editor, Dryad graph save and the one-frame preview; prefab-smoke, hierarchy-smoke, components-smoke, viewport-smoke and tabs-smoke cover the rest. It loads the editor fixture, renames through the real text input, adds an entity, drives the camera and asserts the console:

bash
cd doppio
iced-mcp run-script .iced-mcp/scripts/editor-smoke.luau \
  --launch "./target/debug/doppio ../assets/benchmarks/dense_outdoor.caf"

scripts/doppio-agent.sh builds the C ABI and launches the same app with ICED_MCP=1 for an interactive agent session.

MaterialCraft headless bridge#

bash
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  inspect ../assets/vegetation-kit/materials/celandine_01.mcmat
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  import material.mcmat --out imported/
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  import-sbs material.sbs --out imported/
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  export materials/paint.mat --out paint.mcmat
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  bake-graph materials/paint.mgraph --size 2048 --out maps/
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  texset-info painted.texset
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  texset-new --out painted.texset --size 1024
cargo run -p doppio-ui --bin doppio-material -- \
  texset-export painted.texset --out maps/ --preset "glTF ORM"

The CLI and editor MCP actions share materialcraft_io; the portable export validates its own SBS node/link round-trip and reports imported placeholders.

Session teardown keeps the SDL GPU device for the process lifetime on purpose: SDL_DestroyGPUDevice unloads Vulkan entry points that the host's wgpu/Iced renderer still holds. Sessions are created rarely, so the editor leaks one small device instead of crashing the host.

  • Keep/extend the engine JSON protocol for scene/component/viewport assertions.
  • Add fixtures for project templates, scenes and component schemas.

Rules#

  • Do not re-add the C++ editor to the live tree; use doppio-archived/ as a behaviour reference only.
  • Add widget ids for anything an agent must find.
  • Prefer snapshots/arrays over per-field FFI calls.
  • Keep the Rust frontend out of the CMake build; scripts/check-rust-ui.sh builds the C ABI first and then the workspace.

Script reference card#

The hover card shows module, signature, parameters, return type, an example and related functions. Ctrl+click on an API name opens its reference page: the caffeine-website checkout when found (CAFFEINE_ENGINE_ROOT or a parent of the executable or working directory), otherwise the public URL is logged. A test checks that every documented entry has a page in the website tree.

Generator recipes#

Generators save generator.* recipe files next to what they bake and reopen them on double-click. Other generators reference recipes through uikit/recipe_ref.rs (slots, seeded cached variants, shared SplitMix64 hashing with the engine's core/Hash.hpp); caf-pack skips recipes as editor-only sources. See generator-recipes.md. The generator headers have a Reseed button (generator.toolbar.reseed, texturegen.toolbar.reseed): new seeds for every seeded node, one undo step.

Script editor assistance#

Hover and Ctrl+click resolve the whole dotted name (caffeine.time.delta from any segment) and also cover language words, lifecycle hooks (onUpdate...) and functions or variables declared in the file. Ctrl+click on a declared name jumps to its declaration; on an API name it opens the reference. Typing offers completions from the API, keywords and the file's own symbols (Up/Down to move, Enter or Tab to accept). The editor also has bracket matching and colours, auto-close and auto-indent, indent guides, folding, sticky scroll, search/replace (Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H), go to line (Ctrl+G), the command palette, multi-cursor (Alt+click), move and duplicate line and comment toggle. All of it is in-process; there is no language server.

Dryad node catalog#

58 nodes. Beyond events, transform, time, input and world: Language / Math (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Negate, Min, Max, Abs, Floor, Ceil, Round, Square Root, Power, Sign, Clamp, Clamp 0..1, Lerp, Inverse Lerp, Smoothstep), Trigonometry (Sine, Cosine, degrees/radians), Compare (Less, Greater, Equal), Logic (And, Or, Not), Engine / Random (Value, Range, Int, Chance), Engine / Input (Mouse X/Y/Delta X/Delta Y, Mouse Button), Engine / Time (Fixed Delta, Frame Count) and Engine / World (This Entity, Is Alive, Distance).

Operators are written fully parenthesised, so the importer reads them back unambiguously. Every native-call node is one row of NATIVE_NODES in uikit/dryad.rs (type, labels, native, argument count, bool output); the pins, emitter, importer and catalog follow from the row. The engine side is 20 new caffeine_math_* natives (DryadRuntimeBindings.cpp, documented in script/api/math.json, tested in tests/test_dryad_host.cpp). Not done: variables and loops (they need exec nodes that own a scope, so the emitter and importer must change) and exec nodes for audio, physics and scene natives.
